item.description:
About the Product Manager role

We are seeking an experienced Product Manager with a proven track record in delivering customer facing digital products. The ideal candidate will have experience in fintech, particularly within the payments landscape, and a strong understanding of how to design and implement API-driven financial solutions.

You'll play a pivotal role in defining and delivering Paystack's South African product roadmap, working cross-functionally with engineers, designers, data analysts, and external partners to build innovative local payment solutions.

Our team is small but highly accomplished, so your voice will be heard and your ideas will make meaningful contributions to the business.

Location: South Africa

We'll trust you to

  • Help define and execute the product strategy and roadmap for South Africa, aligning with Paystack's broader business goals.

  • Drive the decision making process across the full product lifecycle, from discovery and strategy through design, development, launch, and continuous iteration.

  • Collaborate closely with design and engineering teams to deliver high-quality, scalable payment solutions.

  • Create detailed product documentation that teams can execute against - PRDs, merchant communications, product marketing docs, and more.

  • Take ownership of problem-solving, proactively identifying blockers and ensuring timely delivery of objectives.

  • Engage directly with customers to translate their business needs and problems into deliverable solutions.

  • Work with banks, card schemes, and other financial partners to deliver solutions that meet customer needs.

  • Represent Paystack in high-value negotiations and at industry events.

  • Maintain open communication on product priorities, progress, and updates with internal and external stakeholders.

  • Combine qualitative and quantitative insights to inform product decisions and measure success.

  • Ensure exceptional user experiences by continuously refining features based on feedback and performance data.

What it takes to succeed in the role

You:

  • Have excellent organisation skills to ensure your team is focused and operating efficiently.

  • Turn incomplete or conflicting inputs into clear, actionable plans.

  • Are an excellent written communicator - your documents are clear, precise, and structured so teams can act on them without further explanation.

  • Are relentlessly user-focused, passionate about delivering world-class digital experiences.

  • Are a self-starter, equally comfortable leading a team or executing independently and able to operate effectively with limited supervision.

  • Use an evidence-based approach to decision-making.

  • Are comfortable balancing short-term deliverables with long-term strategic vision.

  • Continuously seek to improve processes, products, and team performance.

  • Do whatever it takes to make your product, and your team, successful.

You'll thrive in this role if you have

  • A minimum 5+ years experience in product management, preferably within fintech, payments, or banking environments.

  • Familiarity with APIs, payment integrations, and card scheme operations.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and deliver complex projects end-to-end.

  • Exceptional communication, leadership, and stakeholder management skills.

  • Strong analytical and data-driven decision-making abilities.

  • Hands-on familiarity with AI tools as part of your product workflow - for example, using Claude Code or similar tools to prototype ideas, explore solutions, and accelerate discovery and documentation.

Bonus points if you have

  • An understanding of the South African payments ecosystem, including compliance and regulatory considerations.

  • A degree or qualification in Computer Science, Software Development, or Information Systems.

  • Certification or training in Business Analysis or Product Management (Agile, Scrum, or SAFe methodologies).

  • Experience working across African markets.

item.title: Business Development Manager, South Africa
item.description:
About Paystack

Paystack helps businesses in Africa get paid by anyone, from anywhere in the world. Thousands of businesses, from fast-growing startups to large enterprises, use Paystack to power payments, including Xero, Qatar Airways and many more.

Founded in Nigeria and now active across multiple African markets, Paystack is backed by Stripe and is building the payments infrastructure that will power growth across the continent. In South Africa, we work with ambitious businesses across e-commerce, fintech, retail, logistics, and digital services.

About the Role

The Business Development Manager will be a key contributor to Paystack’s Business Development function in South Africa, reporting directly to the Business Development Lead. You will focus on driving enterprise growth through building and managing a strong pipeline of strategic opportunities.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You will own a defined segment or territory, personally manage complex enterprise sales cycles, and build trusted relationships with key customers. You will bring strong commercial instincts, technical fluency, and the ability to navigate multi-stakeholder deals to close.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

  • Own enterprise pipeline and revenue targets
    Maintain an accurate pipeline, forecast consistently, and hit your targets.

  • Lead complex deal execution
    Own the end-to-end sales cycle for your accounts - from prospecting through close. Manage multi-product, multi-stakeholder engagements with discipline and creativity, knowing which levers to pull to move deals forward.

  • Build and manage senior customer relationships
    Engage with senior decision-makers (CFO, CTO, COO) at key accounts. Understand their business drivers, shape mutually beneficial deal structures, and position Paystack as a trusted payments partner.

  • Bring product and technical depth to the field
    Maintain strong product and technical fluency (APIs, integrations, payments architecture). Use this knowledge to articulate customer requirements internally and co-create solutions with Product and Engineering.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally
    Work closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Support, Legal, and Finance to unlock customer value. Escalate effectively to the Business Development Lead where cross-functional decisions require senior input.

  • Contribute to team learning and standards
    Share market and deal insights proactively. Help raise the bar on sales process discipline, CRM hygiene, and commercial best practices across the team.

The ideal candidate consistently demonstrates the following:

  • Scope & Impact: Accountable for enterprise revenue within a defined territory or segment. Influences deal outcomes and customer relationships through personal execution and commercial expertise.

  • Decision Making: Makes clear, well-reasoned calls on deal strategy and account priorities. Escalates effectively and knows when to bring in the Business Development Lead.

  • Communication & Collaboration: Communicates complex commercial and technical concepts clearly to both customers and internal stakeholders. Builds trust across functions.

  • Pipeline Management: Plans and executes over a full fiscal year with accurate forecasting and disciplined territory coverage. Consistently hits targets.

  • Product Knowledge & Technical Competence: Understands the business and technical drivers of customer requirements, engages credibly at senior levels, and finds win-win deal opportunities for customers and Paystack.

  • Sales Process Execution: Executes the full sales cycle with strong process discipline and an intuitive grasp of what moves deals. Regarded internally as a subject matter expert on enterprise sales.

What We’re Looking For

  • 5+ years in enterprise business development, sales, or strategic account management in high-growth B2B environments (fintech, payments, SaaS, or financial services strongly preferred).

  • Proven track record of owning a territory or segment revenue target and consistently meeting or exceeding goals.

  • Demonstrated success closing complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals in South Africa; comfortable operating at senior executive level.

  • Strong understanding of South Africa’s payments and digital commerce landscape, or the ability to ramp quickly on local market dynamics, regulation, and competitive environment.

  • High technical and product fluency - able to understand APIs, integrations, and payments architecture, and to translate between business and technical stakeholders.

  • Strong CRM discipline, pipeline management, and forecasting capability.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to frame trade-offs and decisions clearly for customers and internal stakeholders.

  • Deep alignment with Paystack’s mission and values.

Nice to Have

  • Direct experience with payment gateways, merchant acquiring, or developer-focused fintech products.

  • Existing senior-level relationships across South African enterprises in Paystack-relevant verticals.

  • Familiarity with modern sales methodologies (e.g., MEDDIC, Challenger) and revenue operations best practices.

Why Join Paystack?

  • High impact: You will directly shape how Paystack wins the South African enterprise market, with scope to own meaningful revenue and customer relationships.

  • Strong backing: Operate with the agility of a growth-stage African fintech.

item.description:

About the Senior Product Manager role

Our team is looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the merchant journey at Paystack, from a merchant's first visit to everyday use.

The role brings onboarding and merchant experience under one owner. Today that journey is shared across many teams and run largely through operations. This role makes it product-led.

You will own onboarding, from signup through KYB decisioning and risk scoring to activation. You will also own the Dashboard, the Merchant App, notifications, webhooks, developer experience, and merchant support and self-serve, across every Paystack market. You will set the standard for what a good merchant experience looks like. Any change that touches merchants, whether it comes from compliance, trust and safety or settlement, passes through this role.

The job is to build systems, not workarounds. A merchant who submits the right information is approved by the next business day, and gets the same good experience every time after that.

The role reports to the Head of Product. It is strongly preferred if the candidate is based in Lagos, Nigeria.

We’ll trust you to

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for merchant onboarding, the Dashboard, the Merchant App, notifications, webhooks, developer experience and merchant self-serve.

  • Own activation end to end, from a merchant's first visit until they are fully using the products they need.

  • Own KYB decisioning and risk scoring at signup, and the rules that decide who is approved, who is reviewed and who is declined.

  • Get every merchant who submits complete, correct information approved by the next business day at the latest.

  • Stop bad submissions at the point of entry by validating documents and data as merchants submit, so at least 98% of submissions need no human fix.

  • Take over the onboarding review automation and extend it, so AI agents and reviewers work in one flow and manual review becomes the exception.

  • Pull verified data from identity, registry and partner sources by API, with the merchant's permission, instead of asking merchants to upload it.

  • Build onboarding as shared infrastructure, with APIs that other Paystack businesses can build their own front ends on.

  • Reactivate dormant merchants, and re-verify merchants whose business or identity details change significantly.

  • Work with Compliance to turn regulatory requirements in each market into rules the system enforces, and let market teams tailor the last mile.

  • Define what good looks like for merchants and hold every team that touches merchants to that standard.

  • Decide how and when merchants hear from Paystack when something happens to their account, money or integration, and build the system that delivers it.

  • Build tooling that plugs into compliance, trust and safety, and settlement systems, and replace manual, case-by-case fixes with self-serve product.

  • Make building on Paystack simple, with clear docs, reliable webhooks, useful logs and a fast path from test to live.

  • Drive adoption of Paystack products with nudges and recommendations, and work with Growth so a better experience turns into more revenue from existing merchants.

  • Track the onboarding funnel and what merchants do in the product, and fix the biggest leaks first.

  • Define and track the metrics: time to approval, first-time-right submission rate, activation rate, and a primary measure of merchant happiness supported by CSAT and NPS.

You’ll thrive in this role if you

  • 7+ years of product management experience shipping customer-facing products, ideally B2B or developer products

  • Experience owning onboarding, KYC/KYB, identity verification or activation products at a payments company, bank or fintech

  • A track record of cutting time to approval or growing activation, with the numbers to show it

  • A strong eye for great experiences, in both product UX and customer experience

  • A sharp front-end and pixel eye, and the discipline to make complex things simple for self-serve users

  • A working understanding of KYB and AML onboarding requirements for payment companies, and how regulators such as the CBN apply them

  • Experience designing decision engines or rules, and the review tooling that sits behind them

  • Strong analytical skills, including funnel analysis and SQL, and the habit of tracking merchant behaviour closely

  • Experience with product-led growth, in-product nudges, recommendations or lifecycle messaging

  • Systems thinking and a habit of fixing the class of problem rather than the single case

  • Technical fluency with APIs, webhooks and developer tools, and the ability to design APIs other teams build on

  • Experience building products for more than one market

  • Sound judgement on the trade-off between speed, conversion and compliance risk, and the confidence to push back on changes that would hurt merchants

  • Prior experience in payments, fintech or merchant platforms, which is a strong asset

About the Senior Product Manager role

Our team is looking for a Senior Product Manager to own trust and safety at Paystack. Merchants trust us with their money, their customers and their accounts. This role keeps them safe.

This is a product role, separate from Paystack's risk and compliance function. That function sets policy and runs reviews and investigations. You build the products and systems that keep merchants safe by design, so protection does not depend on case-by-case intervention.

You will lead a new central Trust & Safety product team. What you build serves every Paystack market, and market teams tailor it to local rules and fraud patterns. The role covers fraud prevention, the security of merchant accounts and API keys, the controls on when merchant funds settle or are held, and ongoing AML and merchant monitoring once a merchant is live. A safe merchant is a merchant who keeps getting paid. A blocked good payment or an unexplained hold hurts a merchant as much as fraud does, so both count against the role.

The role reports to the Head of Product. It is strongly preferred if the candidate is based in Lagos, Nigeria.

We’ll trust you to

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for trust and safety across every Paystack market.

  • Build shared safety infrastructure, including rules, limits, risk scoring, monitoring and case management, that market teams configure for local needs.

  • Stop fraud across cards, bank transfers, direct debit and payouts before money leaves Paystack.

  • Protect merchants from account takeover and leaked API keys, with stronger controls on high-risk actions such as charging saved cards and sending transfers.

  • Own the controls that decide when merchant funds settle, are paused or are held, and make every hold clear to the merchant, with a path to resolve it.

  • Monitor merchants after they go live, and catch sudden changes in volume, velocity or recipients in real time.

  • Build AML, sanctions screening and transaction monitoring that meet regulatory obligations through systems, not manual checks.

  • Tune rules and limits so good transactions go through, and treat every false decline and unnecessary hold as harm to a merchant.

  • Keep fraud rates within card scheme thresholds and avoid scheme fines.

  • Give Paystack's risk and compliance teams the tools to review, investigate and decide quickly, and turn their recurring manual work into product.

  • Give every financial control a clear owner, a roadmap and a metric, so money movement security runs as a product and not as a set of one-off fixes.

  • Lead the product side of fraud incidents, then close the gaps they expose, not just the immediate hole.

  • Work with Merchant Experience & Onboarding, Financial Systems and Core Payments so safety controls plug into their systems and merchants hear about them the right way.

  • Define and track the metrics: fraud loss rate, false decline rate, funds held in error, time to detect, time to contain and funds recovered.

You’ll thrive in this role if you

  • A track record of reducing fraud losses or false declines, with the numbers to show it

  • Experience building rules engines, risk scoring, limits, monitoring or case management tools

  • First-hand knowledge of how fraud works in African payments, including card fraud, account takeover, social engineering and mule accounts

  • A working understanding of AML, sanctions and transaction monitoring obligations for payment companies

  • Strong SQL and data skills, and comfort working with data scientists on models and thresholds

  • Technical fluency with APIs, authentication, event streams and real-time decisioning

  • Experience leading or supporting incident response under pressure

  • A merchant-first view of safety, and sound judgement on the trade-off between protection and conversion

  • The ability to get risk, compliance, legal and engineering teams to agree on one control

  • Clear writing that explains a safety decision to a merchant, an engineer and a regulator

  • Prior experience with acquiring-side or merchant fraud, which is a strong asset

You will own how Paystack responds to, communicates about, remediates and learns from every incident, so that merchants, regulators, leadership and our own teams trust us when things go wrong.

You will own the incident lifecycle across all severities, from intake to closure and retrospective. Functional teams fix the underlying cause; you make sure every incident is owned, communicated, quantified, followed through and closed, and that it does not happen twice. Merchant experience is the lens for every decision: how quickly merchants hear from us, how little they are affected, and how quickly their experience is restored.

The scope covers all incidents company-wide, not only engineering:

  • Platform and partner incidents: outages, degraded success rates and partner downtime (e.g. NIBSS, card schemes)

  • Security and fraud: cyberattacks, card testing and BIN attacks, account compromise

  • Operational loss events: financial losses from process gaps (e.g. pricing errors, reconciliation gaps, counterparty exposure)

  • Compliance and data protection: regulatory, third-party, privacy and AI-related breaches

  • Reputational: negative press or public merchant escalations

You will work closely with Risk, Engineering, Compliance, Finance, CX and Brand. You will report into Operations.

We’ll trust you to

Respond

Make sure every incident is owned, progresses within SLA and is followed through until affected merchants' experience is restored.

  • Incident coordination across all severities: Triage, classify and assign an owner to every incident, with severity driven by merchant impact (e.g. number and tier of merchants affected, payment volume at risk). Lead the response directly for Sev1 and Sev2 (i.e. convene the right people, set the cadence, keep the timeline and decision log); for Sev3 and Sev4, ensure owners progress within SLA.

  • SLA enforcement and escalation: Monitor response and resolution times against severity SLAs, enforce escalation triggers (e.g. Sev2 upgrades to Sev1 after 4 hours without response), and escalate unowned or stalled incidents to line managers.

  • Own remediation: Drive the follow-through, e.g. merchant and partner follow-ups, working with action owners, coordinating refunds, reversals or fund recovery, and confirming fixes hold and merchant issues are resolved before closure.

Communicate

Keep customers and leadership informed with clear, timely and accurate updates, before, during and after an incident.

  • Customer communication: Own merchant and customer communication during and after incidents, i.e. tiered merchant comms, status page, CX and GTM briefings, and closure follow-ups. Merchants should hear from us before they have to ask, and no affected merchant is left without an update until the incident is closed. Maintain pre-approved templates and refresh the crisis comms playbooks with Brand.

  • Executive communication: Keep the OT and leadership informed at the cadence each severity requires, and prepare incident and loss reporting for the board and its risk committee.

  • Regulatory handoff: Flag incidents that may trigger regulatory, scheme or data protection notifications to Risk, who own those notifications, and provide the incident facts and timeline they need.

Learn and improve

Turn every incident into fewer, smaller and better-handled incidents over time.

  • Retrospectives and root cause resolution: Facilitate blameless retrospectives within 5 business days, classify root causes against the taxonomy, assess merchant impact and how well merchants were kept informed, and track remediation to closure. Spot recurring incidents and trends, and drive fixes to the underlying problem, not only the symptom.

  • Loss tracking and risk linkage: Ensure every incident records amount lost, amount recovered and a recovery owner. Work with Risk to quantify losses against risk appetite thresholds and feed control gaps into the risk register.

  • Process refinement: Own the incident management playbook and continuously improve it, i.e. severity criteria, SLAs, escalation paths, function-specific report templates and the system of record.

  • Detection and reporting: Work with Engineering, Risk and Finance so incidents surface through systems, not self-reporting (e.g. alerts, reconciliation breaks, loss thresholds).   • Submit all CBN and NDIC returns accurately and on schedule, and fix the root cause of any late or incorrect filing.

  • Monitor capital adequacy, liquidity ratio, cash reserve requirement and other prudential limits daily, and escalate early when headroom narrows.

  • Apply CBN prudential guidelines for loan classification and provisioning, alongside IFRS 9 expected credit loss models.

  • Represent the bank's finance position in CBN examinations and respond to regulator queries.

Treasury and liquidity

  • Manage daily liquidity, funding and cash positions across settlement, customer deposits and operating accounts.

  • Set and run the bank's investment policy for surplus funds, such as treasury bills, within board-approved limits.

  • Build liquidity stress tests and a contingency funding plan.

Planning, performance and capital

  • Lead the annual budget and rolling forecasts, and report performance against plan to the MD and Board.

  • Model the capital and liquidity impact of new products before launch.

  • Plan capital needs ahead of growth and any change in CBN minimum capital rules.

  • Track product and unit economics, such as net interest margin, cost of funds and cost-to-income ratio.

Tax and compliance

  • Own corporate income tax, VAT, withholding tax and other filings under the current Nigerian tax laws.

  • Manage relationships with tax authorities and advisers, and keep the bank ready for tax audits.

Leadership and governance

  • Present financial and prudential reports to the Board and its Audit and Risk committees.

  • Build and lead a small, high-quality finance team, and set clear standards for accuracy and speed.

  • Work with Risk, Compliance, Engineering and Product so finance processes scale with automation, not headcount.

  • 10+ years in finance, with at least 4 years in a senior finance role at a CBN-licensed bank, microfinance bank or other regulated financial institution.

  • A full professional accounting qualification (ICAN, ACCA, CIMA or CPA), and registration with the Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria.

  • Strong IFRS knowledge, especially IFRS 9 expected credit loss.
